2. The short facts which have given rise to the Rule are as follows:- The plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1973 for declaration of title to the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint and recovery of khas possession thereto in alternate for awarding a money decree of Taka 10,175.10 being the compensation award for the suit land which has been requisitioned by the government for fish seed multiplication farm at Khatlal; that the jotes appertaining to CS Khatian Nos. 385, 718, 1063, 1269 and 1655 of Mouza Khatlal under PS Khetlal, District Bogra belonged to Horekrishna Nath and Ramkrishna Nath in equal share; that the same were recorded in their names correctly in .CS operation; that the said maleks entered into amicable partition of their aforesaid properties after CS operation and in consequence thereof the Ka schedule land measuring 1.72 and 1/2 decimals fell exclusively in the saham of Horekrishna Nath who being in possession thereto died leaving a son Krishna Debnath and a daughter Ananda Sundary; that Sree Krishna Devnath married one Joyananda Sundary and they had no issue, that the Sree Krishna Devnath purchased the 'Kha' schedule property measuring 49 and 1/2 decimals 2 along with other lands in the benami of his wife and since purchase he used to possess the 'Kha' schedule land in his own right, title and interest and that Sree Krishna Devnath being in exclusive possession over the Ka and Kha schedule lands and his wife Jayananda Sundry died. It is further stated that the plaintiffs are sons of Ananda Sundry, the full sister of Sree Krishna Devnath and, as such, they inherited the suit lands along with other properties left by Sree Krishna Devnath as his legal heirs and since then they used to possess the same in their own right, title and interest; that on 15th Ashar 1374 BS corresponding to 30-7-67 AD, the local Tahshildar of Khatlal threatened the Bargadars of the plaintiffs to dispossess therefrom on the plea that the properties left by Sree Krishna Devnath were taken overby the government as he left no heirs and that the plain- tiffs are not legal heirs of the deceased Sree Krishna Devnath. 

 14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the evidence on record I am of the view that the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge on the point for maintainability of the suit is correct and there is nothing to argue against the same. Admittedly the suit property has been requisitioned by the government of Bangladesh for seed multiplication farm and it has been permanently acquired. So the findings that the suit for declaration of title over the suit properties and recovery of khas possession by evicting the defendant therefrom is a bar under section 14A of the Requisition of Property Act. The learned Assistant Attorney General for the State did not press this point inasmuch as, she conceded the legal position. So the only point left is to ascertain as to whether the plaintiffs are heirs of Sree Krishna Devnath. Admittedly the suit land belonged to Sree Krishna Devnath. The plaintiff's case is supported by oral and documentary evidence and it has been proved that the plaintiffs are the sons of Ananda Sundary, the full sister of Krishna Devnath. It is also admitted that Krishna Devnath and his wife died issueless. PW 1 stated as it appears on perusal of his evidence thatthe plaintiffs are son of Ananda Sundary. There is no denial on the point. It further appears from the evidence of PW-2, a local Prodhan, that plaintiffs are the heirs of Sree Krishna Devnath being sons of his full sister Ananda Sundary. He has also said that the amicable partition as alleged in the plaint took place in his presence and that the plaintiffs used to possess the suit land as well as other properties left by Sree KrishnaDevnath as his heirs. It further appears from the certified copy of the decree Exhibit-3 that the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 141 of 67 before the Court of 3rd Munsif, Bogra against the then government of East Pakistan for permanent injunction restraining the defendants of that suit from disturbing their peaceful possession over the properties left by Sree Krishna Dev Nath and that the present suit lands were included thereto. In that suit the plaintiffs claimed themselves as legal heirs of late Krishna Devnath being sons of full sister of the deceased and also claimed to be in exclusive possession of the properties left by Sree Krishna Devnath who died issueless.
